## Rule

**DECODED 2026-06-01 (v1 rewrite — 100% / 200,000 vs ARC-GEN GT, exactly matches LIVE):**

A bordered rectangle: **A** = frame color (the non-bg color whose cells are 4-connected adjacent to background), **B** = inner fill color (the other non-bg color, strictly interior — never touches bg). The fill rectangle has a small defect, and a "cross-out" is drawn through it; cleared cells become **B** where the cell was background, else **A**. Two defect modes (the generator produces both):

1. **Sparse markers** — one or more rows/cols of B are sparse (B-count < ⅔·max). A B-cell in a sparse *row* clears its *column* (vertical line); a B-cell in a sparse *col* clears its *row* (horizontal line). This covers isolated B-pixels protruding into the frame.
2. **Corner notch** (no sparse markers) — a single 1-cell dent at a corner of the B rectangle. Then cross **all the FULL lines** (B-count == max) along the **shorter bbox dimension** (e.g. a 4×6 bbox with a notch → cross the full rows; a 10×4 bbox → cross the full cols).

The cross paints a full line across the grid: background margins → B, frame/fill cells on the line → A. Padding (outside the active H×W grid) stays all-zero.

**Historical trap (still valid):** `Research_Archive/notes/digest-task383-2026-05-11.md` — the old `task383_v2` was a visible-derived axis-cross-out that matched 266/266 visible but was **hidden-bad** on Kaggle (−12.31 LB). The difference now: the v1 rewrite is validated at **100% against 200k ARC-GEN ground-truth samples** (the hidden distribution), not just the 266 visible pairs, and matches LIVE 266/266. Decode-from-visible-only is the trap; decode-and-verify-against-the-generator is safe.

The current best task383 graph is the exact-LIVE topology FP16 repair (`task383_v3_topology_fp16` lineage): it keeps the live axis-cross-out/anomaly-marker topology and uses FP16 float tensors. This cursor sweep did not rederive the rule. It tested ONNX broadcasting rewrites that replace constant all-one/all-zero tensors with rank-0 FP16 scalar initializers, then compared candidate outputs against the current-live task383 graph.

## Cost analysis

**v6 #98 dilated conv (2026-06-11): cost 10,942 = memory 10,856 + params 86 (points ~15.70). Δ −2,170 vs v5 13,112. Byte-equal to v5/LIVE (ab --full 200266/200266).** (Progression: v1 25,767 → v3 18,666 → v5 13,112 → **v6 10,942**.) The dilated Conv K[1,10,2,2] dilation=6 crops the 30×30 color-decode directly to 24×24 F32 (2,304 B) — replaces cidx_full (3,600 B) + cidx_u30 (900 B). Net memory −2,196; net params +26 (kernel [1,10,2,2]=40 vs old color_w [1,10,1,1]=10 + crop_e[4] removed).

**v8 corrected free-output BitwiseAnd tail (2026-06-21): cost 9,148 = memory 9,010 + params 138, profile 9,148.** This is the cheapest correct Boladi formulation measured in the Where-overlay/free-output family this pass, but it is still **+1,806 above Aditya team-best 7,342**, so it is not staged. It deletes v6's 900-B `canvas30` and the 24x24 output-color planes by generating the full one-hot as `BitwiseAnd(rowbits [1,10,30,1] U8, colbits [1,1,1,30] U8) == output`. The corrected decomposition needs 7 row/col products: two A rectangle-complement terms, three B terms (interior + horizontal/vertical bg stripes), and two channel-0 background-completeness terms. Dominant charged tensors still left: `cidx_f24` 2,304 B, `is_B_h` 1,152 B, `cidx_u` 576 B, `is_B_b` 576 B, plus `rowbits`/row channel-select 1,020 B. The prompt's single-Where overlay is not cheap here because there are **two data-dependent replacement colors** (A inside rectangle, B on background stripes) and channel-0 background must remain complete; a nested full-canvas `Where` would materialize a 10-channel intermediate, while the bitset tail is the cheaper exact free-output form.

**v5 rewrite (2026-06-02): cost 13,112 = memory 13,052 + params 60 (points 15.52).** (Superseded by v6.) v5's per-tensor breakdown is in the floor proof below. The earlier v3 breakdown (kept for reference):

| 1,152 | `is_B_h` | [1,1,24,24] F16 | B-mask fed to `ReduceSum` for counts. `ReduceSum` has no UINT8/int8 kernel; F16 (2 B) is the smallest. **Forced.** |
| 900×2 | `cidx_u30`, `out30u` | [1,1/30,30] U8 | the two 30-wide bridges (U8 cast before the 24-crop; padded U8 index before the INT32 cast). Both alternatives measured larger. |
| 576 each (×12) | per-cell masks | [1,1,24,24] U8/BOOL | the 12 essential per-cell stages: color index, nonbg, is_B (+U8/F16 casts), 2 marker masked-products, cleared, cleared-color, paint, sentinel, reshape, active. Each is 576 B because the **active grid reaches 24×24** (verified all 200k pairs; sub-24 fails hidden per traps §CROP-CONTRACT). |

### Floor proof (revised 2026-06-11 after #98 dilated conv — empirical, formulation-relative)

The chain drove 55,467 → 25,767 → 18,666 → 13,112 → **10,942** via real structural rewrites. The #98 dilated conv (v6) eliminated `cidx_full` (3,600 B) and `cidx_u30` (900 B), replacing them with `cidx_f24` [1,1,24,24] F32 (2,304 B). What remains in v6:

| bytes | tensor | forced by |
|---:|---|---|
| 2,304 | `cidx_f24` [1,1,24,24] F32 | the per-cell **color decode**. ORT `Conv` is float-only (outputs F32); the dilated conv crops directly to 24×24 (technique #98) — 1,296 B cheaper than the old 30×30 bridge. Cannot narrow further: no F16 Conv kernel; Cast to U8 is next. |
| 1,152 | `is_B_h` [1,1,24,24] F16 | the per-cell **B-count**. `ReduceSum`/`MatMul` have no sub-F16 kernel. |
| 900 | `canvas30` [1,1,30,30] U8 | the output canvas (already at the §238 single-channel floor). |

**These three (4,356 B) are set by ORT op-dtype kernels**, plus the 576-B `cidx_u` U8 crop and ~6k of 24×24 per-cell masks (cidx, is_B, cleared, clr_c, paint, sentinel, active — each 576 B, forced by the 24×24 active grid). Total v6 memory = 10,856.

**Realistic floor ~10.9k.** The forced color-decode (2,304 F32 + 576 U8) + B-count (1,152 F16) + output canvas (900 U8) = 4,932 B; with the minimal per-cell mask set (~5,952 B) total is ≈10,884 B. The v6 params (86) are driven by the dilated kernel (40) plus the index/reshape scalars (46). No further structural reformulation has been identified: the `cidx_f24` size is already the minimum ORT-achievable (24×24×4 B); cutting it further would require a non-float Conv or a completely different color-read strategy.

Also: duplicate indices at the row/col intersections make ScatterND write-order ONNX-unspecified (hidden-bad hazard; task383 has −12.31 LB history). The two-stage strip design is the scatter floor.
- **Don't try to Gather A/B channels out of the F32 one-hot to delete the color-decode Conv** (the 2026-06-22 re-attack angle). `Gather(input, idx, axis=channel)` inherits the **F32** input dtype → the channel slice is F32 [1,1,30,30]=3,600 B (2,304 B cropped) PER CHANNEL, not a U8 mask. A minimal Gather-channel skeleton (two channels, no cross-out logic) measured 16,196 = 2.2× the whole team-best. The dilated #98 Conv is the floor: it produces ONE 2,304-B F32 plane carrying the full color index (serves bbox + A/B values + marker detect + scatter canvas); the Gather angle needs TWO F32 planes and is strictly worse. ConvInteger/QLinearConv reject F32 input and need a 9,000-B full-input U8 cast first.

The prompt's premise — "input is one-hot **U8**" — is **FALSE**: the NeuroGolf model input is **F32** [1,10,30,30] (verified `elem_type=1`). To weight channels by an iota you need a `Mul(input, iota)` BEFORE the channel reduce, and that Mul materializes the full 10-channel weighted plane = F32 [1,10,30,30] = **36,000 B** (probed: `score_v2=42,502`, dominant intermediate `weighted` 36,000 B). `ReduceMax` then outputs the input dtype (F32 3,600 → cropped 2,304) — the *same* 2,304-B F32 plane the Conv already produces, just with 36k of junk in front. The Conv `K[1,10,2,2]` is structurally superior: it **fuses** weight-and-sum in ONE op so the 10-channel weighted tensor is never materialized. Casting input→U8 first to keep the reduce in U8 costs a 9,000-B U8 `[1,10,30,30]` cast = still worse. **Conv is the per-cell color-decode floor; no channel-reduce (ReduceMax/ReduceSum/Mul) beats it because all require materializing the weighted 10-channel plane.** Probe: `task383/prototypes/probe_reducemax_u8.py`.

Not comparable to task181/335/203 low-k (those tasks have smaller active grids / no per-cell color index). The old v5 "floor ~13k" claim was superseded by v6 (10,942) via #98.

The corrected v8 `BitwiseAnd` tail is exact on visible + 2k truth/AB and profile-stable, but costs 9,148; it does not beat Aditya's 7,342 unless a separate formulation deletes the F32 color decode or F16 B-count plane.
- **DO make the `Equal(canvas, channel_ids)` BOOL result the graph OUTPUT** (not an intermediate) — the §238 single-channel-canvas pattern. This beats `OneHot` (saves the 3,600-byte INT32 index). The trap: do NOT `Cast` the Equal to F32 afterward (that makes the 10-ch Equal a 9,000-byte intermediate — that was v4_ohfree's 24,977 mistake). Declare `output` as BOOL; the validator decodes `result>0`, gates pass (visible 266/266, truth 200k/200k).
- **Marker cross via MatMul on the F16 B-mask** (`mk_cols[c]=Σ_r anom_row[r]·is_B[r,c]`) has tiny [1,1,1,24] outputs and reuses `is_B_h` — removes the per-direction 24×24 masked planes. Beats `Where`+`ReduceMax`.
- **A/B color shortcut (verified 0/200k):** frame A = `cidx` at the first NON-BG cell `(r0,c0)`; fill B = `cidx` at the NON-BG bbox center `((r0+r1)//2,(c0+c1)//2)`. Get r0/r1/c0/c1 via `ArgMax`(+`select_last_index=1`) of `Greater(ReduceMax(cidx_u, axis), 0)` (NOT of `ReduceMax(input)` — that marks the whole grid incl. bg margins, so the corner lands on bg). Then `is_B = Equal(cidx, B_sc)` directly (no adjacency masks). This replaced the whole MaxPool A-detect chain.
- **Compute the cross "cleared" mask at the VECTOR level:** `cleared_rows[H]`/`cleared_cols[W]` are tiny; combine marker-vs-notch on the vectors and do ONE outer-`Or` for the single 24×24 mask. Materializing per-cell marker/notch/combine planes (v1) wasted ~2,880 bytes.
- **Don't use the simple "sparse line, count*3<max*2" rule alone** — it's 99.884% (misses 232/200k corner-notch cases where the defect is a 1-cell corner dent that doesn't make any line sparse enough). The corner-notch fallback (cross full lines along the shorter bbox dim when no sparse markers exist) is REQUIRED for 100%. Raising the sparse threshold does NOT help (0.8 → 96.9%, over-triggers; tested full-corpus).
- **Don't omit the active-region sentinel mask** — our 24×24 canvas paints cross-out rays across the whole crop, but LIVE/GT leave padding (outside the actual H×W) all-zero. Without masking padding to the OneHot out-of-range sentinel (index 10), the visible gate is 0/266 (all-zero-padding vs channel0=1 mismatch). Factor active = row_has AND col_has via per-axis `ReduceMax(input,axes=[1,3])` (tiny [1,1,30,1] outputs), not a full `ReduceMax(input,axes=[1])` (3,600).
- **ORT op-dtype gotchas hit this build:** `ReduceSum` no UINT8 (use F16), `ReduceMax` OK on UINT8 but NOT on BOOL, `Mul`/`Sub` no UINT8, `Where` data branches can't be BOOL (cast to U8), `OneHot` indices must be INT32 with matching INT32 depth (int8/16/uint8 all `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`). `OneHot` out-of-range index → all-zero channels (used as the padding sentinel). `Pad` rejects BOOL.
